parts.label: (a)
hints: Hint 1: Start by recalling how an ideal op-amp used open-loop decides its output - what comparison of $V_+$ and $V_-$ gives $+5.0\text{ V}$ and what gives $-5.0\text{ V}$?
Hint 2: Think about what voltages you can make from the battery on the left - how can two resistors between the top wire and the earthed bottom wire give a fixed reference voltage at one input?
Hint 3: Remember an NTC thermistor has high resistance when cold and low resistance when hot - which position in a divider (top or bottom) will make the divider voltage fall as temperature rises?
Hint 4: Check your choice gives $V_- > V_+$ at low temperature for $-5.0\text{ V}$ output and $V_+ > V_-$ at high temperature for $+5.0\text{ V}$ output.
parts.proper_answer: Two potential dividers connected between top of battery and earthed bottom wire. Divider 1: two $1000\,\Omega$ resistors in series, midpoint to $V_+$. Divider 2: $1000\,\Omega$ resistor (top) in series with thermistor (bottom to earth), midpoint to $V_-$. At low T $V_- > V_+$, at high T $V_- < V_+$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **How the comparator switches**
Think of the op-amp here as a simple comparer with huge gain. If $V_+ > V_-$ the output saturates high at about $+5.0\text{ V}$. If $V_- > V_+$ it saturates low at about $-5.0\text{ V}$. So you need one input to be a fixed reference and the other to move with temperature and cross over it.

Step 2: **Make a fixed reference with two resistors**
Join the top battery wire to the top of two $1000\,\Omega$ resistors in series, with the bottom of the chain to earth. The midpoint is: $$V_+ = V_{battery} \times \frac{1000}{1000+1000} = 0.5 V_{battery}$$ This stays constant and goes to the non-inverting (+) input.

Step 3: **Make a sensing divider with the thermistor**
Join the same top battery wire to a $1000\,\Omega$ resistor, then to the NTC thermistor down to earth. Take the midpoint to the inverting (-) input: $$V_- = V_{battery} \times \frac{R_{therm}}{1000 + R_{therm}}$$ An NTC resistor is large when cold and small when hot, so $V_-$ is high when cold and low when hot.

Step 4: **Check the switching works**
At low T, $R_{therm} > 1000\,\Omega$ so $V_- > 0.5V_{battery} = V_+$, giving $V_{OUT} = -5.0\text{ V}$. At high T, $R_{therm} < 1000\,\Omega$ so $V_- < V_+$, giving $V_{OUT} = +5.0\text{ V}$. That is exactly the required temperature switch.

parts.label: (b)(i)
hints: Hint 1: For $V_{OUT} = -5.0\text{ V}$ you need $V_- > V_+$, so with the circuit above does the thermistor resistance need to be larger or smaller than the $1000\,\Omega$ fixed resistor?
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Cold means high resistance**
At low temperature you need $V_- > V_+ = 0.5V_{battery}$. From $$V_- = V_{battery} \frac{R_{therm}}{1000+R_{therm}}$$ this needs $R_{therm} > 1000\,\Omega$. Any value clearly above $1000\,\Omega$, for example about $1500$ to $5000\,\Omega$, is suitable.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: For $V_{OUT} = +5.0\text{ V}$ you need $V_+ > V_-$, so as the NTC warms up in which direction must its resistance change relative to $1000\,\Omega$?
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Hot means low resistance**
At higher temperature you need $V_- < V_+$. This needs $R_{therm} < 1000\,\Omega$. Any value clearly below $1000\,\Omega$, for example about $100$ to $800\,\Omega$, is suitable and shows the NTC resistance has fallen.
